subject: Political Science
central_question: How do domestic political developments, conflicts and regional cooperation shape contemporary South Asia?
in_scope_units: Meaning and political diversity of South Asia
Ethnic conflict and democracy in Sri Lanka
Peace and cooperation through SAARC and SAFTA
Role of external powers in South Asia
banned_topics: Detailed evolution of the European Union
India’s domestic party system after Independence

known_pitfalls.claim: Every South Asian country has followed the same democratic path.
known_pitfalls.correction: The region has a mixed record that includes stable democracy, monarchy, military rule and democratic transitions.

known_pitfalls.claim: SAARC has removed all political conflicts in the region.
known_pitfalls.correction: SAARC promotes cooperation, but bilateral disputes and political differences have limited its effectiveness.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Exercise 2: Which among the following statements about South Asia is wrong? a) All the countries in South Asia are democratic. b) Bangladesh and India have signed an agreement on river-water sharing. c) SAFTA was signed at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad. d) The US and China play an influential role in South Asian politics.
NCERT Exercise 3: What are some of the commonalities and differences between Bangladesh and Pakistan in their democratic experiences?
NCERT Exercise 5: Name the principal players in the ethnic conflict in Sri Lanka. How do you assess the prospects of the resolution of this conflict?

NCERT Exercise 10: India’s neighbours often think that the Indian government tries to dominate and interfere in the domestic affairs of the smaller countries of the region. Is this a correct impression?
NCERT Exercise 9: Write a short note on the role and the limitations of SAARC as a forum for facilitating economic cooperation among the South Asian countries.
